title: Pre-AGI AI Action Governance: Governing Autonomous Authority, Scale, and Consequential Action Before AGI
description: Pre-AGI AI Action Governance is a research and policy framework for governing consequential autonomous AI action without waiting for artificial general intelligence. The framework shifts the primary governance focus from model intelligence alone toward autonomous authority, access, scale, persistence, external action, consequence, verification, and accountability. It introduces four core concepts: Scale-Looping Power, the Autonomous Impact Threshold, the AI Action Accountability Stack, and the Governance Target Selection Problem. Its central principle is that intelligence does not imply authority: model evaluation should inform governance, action capability should trigger governance, and consequence should determine governance intensity.
notes: This repository develops a practical pre-AGI governance framework centered on autonomous authority and consequential action rather than intelligence level alone. Core principles include: Intelligence does not imply authority; AI autonomy must not break the chain of accountability; model evaluation informs governance; action capability triggers governance; consequence determines governance intensity; and stronger autonomous impact requires stronger structural control.
